title: Coordinate algebras with scheme-groupoid descent data
statement: Let $U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $(s,t,e,i,c)$ a scheme groupoid [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. In an ambient universe containing their rings of global functions, put $E=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, $L=\Gamma(R,\mathcal O_R)$. Define the category of commutative $E$-algebras $A$ with an $L$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:A\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}L\simeq A\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The identity pullback of $\beta$ is the identity, and transport along two composable arrows composes to transport along $c$. Equivalently these equations hold on points valued in every commutative ring in the ambient universe: a transport from $x$ to $y$ over $r:L\to C$ means that $(x,r)=(y,r)\circ\beta$. Morphisms are all $E$-algebra maps commuting with transport. Tensor products are represented by ring pushouts with their specified inclusions. The invariant subring of $A$ is $\{a:\beta(a\otimes1)=a\otimes1\}$. No finiteness hypothesis is imposed on $A$. For affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the canonical global-function isomorphisms recover the given coordinate rings.
